subject: Model fit prompt warehouse & redaction checklist
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Hart <sam.hart@aureliadiagnostics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Model fit prompt warehouse & redaction checklist

Hi Sam —

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for walking us through your user flows for clinical note summarization and the triage assistant. Quick recap + asks so we can kick off a lightweight eval: 

1) Goal: validate model quality on your production prompts and identify any quality regressions after any model/profile changes.
2) Deliverables from Aurelia we need to run an initial fit eval:
   - ~200 representative prompts (short and long clinical notes; include both edge cases and normal cases)
   - An example of expected output (gold/annotated) for ~30 prompts if available
   - A short list of redaction constraints (what counts as PHI in your context)

I've attached a prompt_samples_template.csv you can use to drop samples into (column headers + guidance included). Also attached: a doc with our suggested redaction levels if you want a starting point.

Quick asks / next steps:
- Can you upload the CSV to the secure folder link below by EOD Thu (11/18)?
- Tell us whether outputs will be used for human review vs. direct downstream actions (this affects model safety thresholds).
- If you have strict PHI rules beyond standard HIPAA categories, flag them here.

Secure upload: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1a2B_prompt-warehouse-recs (or reply with a DocuSign/secure transfer preference)

I'll loop in Marissa for model recommendations and an initial benchmark plan. If you'd like, we can provision a test endpoint on Redwood Dedicated for a 48-hour sanity run once we have samples.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: prompt_samples_template.csv] [Attachment: redaction_guidelines_v2.docx]

From: Sam Hart <sam.hart@aureliadiagnostics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@aureliadiagnostics.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Model fit prompt warehouse & redaction checklist

Ben —

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifying questions before we pull the prompts together:

1) PHI: we have three tiers — direct identifiers (names, MRNs), quasi-identifiers (zip + age > 89), and free-text clinical observations. We need PHI redaction on direct identifiers for any data we send to hosted endpoints; for Dedicated/private testing we can relax that.
2) Expected output golds: we can provide about 20 annotated summaries next week; do you need them in a specific schema?
3) Timeline: we can target Thu (11/18) for an initial batch upload but need an NDA addendum for any sample logs to be retained beyond 30 days.

—Sam
Sam Hart
Head of Data & Integrations
Aurelia Diagnostics
[Attachment: internal_policy_excerpts.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Hart <sam.hart@aureliadiagnostics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Model fit prompt warehouse & redaction checklist

Hi Sam —

Thanks — quick model + benchmark plan so you have context while you prep samples. High-level recommendations based on the workload you described (clinical summarization, triage assistant):

Recommended model candidates (for evaluation):
- redwood-instruct-7b-q4f: best cost/throughput tradeoff for batch evals; expect higher factuality with careful prompt engineering.
- redwood-alpha-1.1-8k: stronger on longer-context summarization and instruction following; higher cost.
- rw-quant-13b-8k (quantized profile): try for edge-case robustness if latency and budget allow.

Benchmarks / metrics we'll run:
- ROUGE/F1 against your golds (for structured summary metrics)
- Human-rated faithfulness + hallucination index (annotator rubric we can share)
- Regression tests using your edge-case set (we'll flag any >10% degradation vs baseline)

Prompt set guidance (columns in the template):
- prompt_id, original_text, user_intent_label, expected_summary, redaction_needed(boolean), notes_on_edge_case

Security/compliance notes: for any samples with direct identifiers we recommend either:
- uploading to your Private deployment (we can provide instructions), or
- replace identifiers with consistent tokens (e.g., [PATIENT_123]) and provide a mapping offline for internal evals.

I'll drop a short eval workbook to the shared folder with metric definitions and a sample scoring sheet. Once we have the samples we can provision a 48-hour Dedicated endpoint and run the candidate models in parallel.

Links: evaluation workbook (view only) - https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1a2B_prompt-warehouse-recs

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering (Model Ops)
Redwood Inference

Sam —

Quick follow to confirm logistics and attachments:

- We can accept tokenized prompts (preferred) or samples sent to a Private sandbox. If tokenized, please keep the token substitution consistent across examples so our eval can measure entity coherence.
- Attached are the two files again: prompt_samples_template.csv and redaction_guidelines_v2.docx. Use the template header exactly as-is to avoid parsing issues.
- Upload path (secure): https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1a2B_prompt-warehouse-recs. If you need SFTP instead, let us know and we'll open a temporary account.
- NDA addendum: I've looped in Aditya to fast-track a 30-day sample retention clause. Aditya — can you confirm we can sign the addendum and keep samples for 30 days maximum for evaluation?

Thanks — aiming to start the model run on Mon (11/21) if we get the samples by Thu.

Ben
